solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Backing for climb from degree taking short time to being in the House

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
a sec, short for second, is a brief moment
a being in the House of Commons is a Member of Parliament: A MP

explanation.surface: A climber's support is pieced together from a degree, a brief moment and a parliamentarian.
explanation.walkthrough: The article must be read into 'being': a being in the House is A MP. Fifteensquared commenters noted the A is only implied.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineering expedition is supported from its lowest staging camp, where supplies are kept.

clue.text: Sexually ambiguous mushrooms with muscle

parts.note: bi, short for bisexual, attracted to both sexes
ceps are edible boletus mushrooms, porcini

explanation.surface: A gym-goer of uncertain orientation eats fungi to build muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm's two-headed flexor in the upper arm is a well-known muscle.

clue.text: Sun on cathedral and nowhere else?

parts.note: Sol is the Latin and poetic name for the sun
Ely, a city in Cambridgeshire, is the crossword's favourite cathedral

explanation.surface: Is the sun shining on this cathedral and on nowhere else?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places SOL above ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Only, exclusively: something done in one place and nowhere else is done there alone.

clue.text: Lady of the Lake with attitude

parts.note: con is Italian and Spanish for with, as in chilli con carne
a stance is a stated position or attitude

explanation.surface: A lady from an Arthurian lake behaves with plenty of attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lady of the Lake suggests Arthurian legend, but here she is a woman's name shared with Lake Constance on the Swiss-German-Austrian border.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a woman's name and also the name of the large Alpine lake on the Rhine.

clue.text: Show good girls the harmonica

parts.note: a musical is a stage show with songs
lasses are girls, chiefly in Scottish and northern English

explanation.surface: A stage show features good girls playing a mouth organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harmonica' suggests a mouth organ, but the glass harmonica was a set of tuned glass bowls played with wet fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuned drinking glasses rubbed with damp fingers form the instrument Benjamin Franklin developed as the glass harmonica.

clue.text: Shiner to be a Tory?

parts.note: taken as the verb be
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether being a Conservative makes one a shining light.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal fire or lighthouse lamp shines out to guide or warn people.

clue.text: Panic doesn't start by mistake

indicators.note: the word for panic loses its opening letter

parts.note: terror is extreme fear, a state of panic

explanation.surface: Someone panics after setting something off by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or blunder is an inaccuracy or mistake.

clue.text: Something spicy to read about pub in the morning

indicators.note: the word for read goes about the pub and the morning, split open around them

parts.note: to con is to study or read over closely
an inn is a pub
a.m., ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone reads up on a spiced breakfast at the pub in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic bark of a tropical tree is a common sweet spice.

clue.text: Novice making a mess of one contest, say

indicators.note: messing up the word one jumbles its letters
say signals that a word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a fight is a contest

explanation.surface: A beginner fouls up a single competition.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE is rearranged as NEO; FIGHT, spoken, is spelt PHYTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner or new convert, a novice in some field.

clue.text: Singer finding the spot for love protects one old bird getting married

indicators.note: the outer string wraps around and shields the inner pieces

parts.note: placing something is finding the spot for it
I is the Roman numeral for one
the dodo is an extinct bird
love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A singer finds a place for love that shelters an old bird getting wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Protects' puts IDODOM inside PLACINGO, splitting it as PLAC...INGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Plácido Domingo is the celebrated Spanish operatic tenor, one of the Three Tenors.

clue.text: So someone borrows California's Roman date?

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
if someone borrows, it is because another lends

explanation.surface: Someone borrows a Californian Roman calendar date.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinephile's logic: if the state lends, then so someone borrows; 'So someone borrows' is the consequence, not a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The calends were the first day of each month in the Roman calendar.

clue.text: Venetian lover takes Italian actor to Australia another way

parts.note: Sophia Loren is a famous Italian film actress

indicators.note: taking the word for Australia the other way round turns it back to front

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: An Italian actor travels to Australia by a different route.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Merchant of Venice, Lorenzo elopes with Shylock's daughter Jessica.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Lorenzo lives in Venice and woos and elopes with Jessica.

clue.text: Guide to too good a fate

parts.note: pi, short for pious, describes someone sanctimoniously good
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: Something guides people to a destiny too good to be true.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steers a ship into harbour, or a guide in general, is a pilot.

clue.text: Bird, fish, and so-called beetle

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A list names a bird, a fish and something called a beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' is fair because this insect is popularly called a black beetle but is not a beetle at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The household pest is often loosely called a black beetle though it belongs to a different order.

clue.text: I'm uncle, due to poor Goldwyn's refusal to take part

indicators.note: poor handling of the words leaves them disordered

parts.note: taken as the letters I and M

explanation.surface: A family member regrets being in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: Hollywood producer Sam Goldwyn was famed for malapropisms such as this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Goldwyn's famous mangled phrase means he would not participate.

clue.text: Major confusion of other mortals with me

indicators.note: the letters are made into something other than they were

explanation.surface: Mixing other people with oneself causes great confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool, figuratively a scene of violent turmoil or confusion.

clue.text: Greek hero's headless corpse on ship with headless god

indicators.note: a headless word loses its first letter

parts.note: a body is a corpse
SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: again, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Zeus is chief of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A headless corpse lies aboard a ship beside a beheaded god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless' twice removes B from BODY and Z from ZEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The wily king of Ithaca is the hero of Homer's Odyssey.

clue.text: Intrude upon that beetle's better 'alf?

annotationWithheld.why: Intrude upon that beetle's better 'alf? (8): the joke turns COCKROACH's cock into its mate ('EN) but leaves a stray C to give ENCROACH; no parse makes the letters, and the blog's commenters call it an error

clue.text: Providers for the youthful stomach, possibly — indies

indicators.note: the word indies is read as in dies, putting the first piece within the word dies

parts.note: taken as written
a boy's insides: his inner, plus lad for a youth

explanation.surface: Independent record labels might provide nourishment for youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indies' splits as IN DIES, so INNER LAD goes inside DIES; 'possibly' warns the stomach phrase is loosely built.
explanation.definitionFit: School canteen staff serve lunch to children, providing their midday meal.

clue.text: Whither good news was brought in article about persistent pain

indicators.note: the article is placed around the pain

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
an ache is a dull, continuing pain

explanation.surface: An article about chronic pain also mentions where good news was carried.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning's poem How They Brought the Good News from Ghent to Aix ends at Aix, the French name for this city.
explanation.definitionFit: Aix-la-Chapelle, destination of the riders in Browning's poem, is the German city of that name.

clue.text: Magic potion: 'as garden mollusc got one right?

indicators.note: the dropped h of 'as shows the mollusc's name loses its h too

parts.note: Helix is the genus of the common garden snail
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A garden snail somehow has a magic potion that puts one right.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney 'as for has signals dropping the H, so HELIX becomes ELIX.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a supposed magical draught, such as the elixir of life.

clue.text: Artists back fuel all consisting of seaweed

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, artists
gas is a fuel
the sum is the whole, all of it

explanation.surface: Artists return fuel made entirely from seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: The floating brown algae that names the Sargasso Sea is a seaweed.

clue.text: Trembler causing broken panes

indicators.note: the pane letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Something shaking makes window panes break.
explanation.walkthrough: The trembling poplar is named for its quivering leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This poplar's leaves quiver in the slightest breeze, hence its Latin name tremula.

clue.text: Garden mollusc's second fx

parts.note: fx is the blog's dropped-letter copy of fix; to fix something is to nail it

explanation.surface: A garden pest gets a second fix.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'fix'; the source copy lost its i.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelled gastropod that eats garden plants is the familiar pest.

clue.text: Former partner with more than suffcient specimen

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means more than enough (sufficient is misspelt in the copy)

explanation.surface: A former partner has more than enough of a specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a sample or instance typical of its kind.

clue.text: Direction and skill needed to spell church portico

parts.note: N is north, a compass direction
art is skill
a hex is a spell or curse

explanation.surface: Instructions and craft are needed to spell out a church porch.
explanation.definitionFit: The antechamber or porch at a church's west end is called the narthex.

clue.text: Southern pub, home to unknown puzzler

parts.note: PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub
in means at home
x is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A southern pub hosts a mysterious riddler.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sphinx of Thebes posed a riddle to travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: The riddling monster of Greek myth posed a famous puzzle to Oedipus.

clue.text: No royal arrival to embrace Scotsman

indicators.note: the arrival wraps round the Scotsman

parts.note: a comer is one who arrives
mon is a stereotypical Scots address for man

explanation.surface: A new arrival hugs a Scotsman with no royal connections.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone not of the nobility or royalty is an ordinary member of the public.
